correctness.rationale: A length-k factorization corresponds to a word in a copies of p and b copies of q, cut into k weakly increasing nonempty blocks by sorting the prime labels within each factor. Every descent forces a cut, and other gaps may be cut independently. A word with j descents contributes t^(j+1)(1+t)^(a+b−1−j); its descending corners in the lattice-word path select j distinct abscissas and j distinct ordinates, giving binom(a,j)binom(b,j) words. The resulting finite sum is exactly the standard shifted Jacobi binomial formula times t(1+t)^(M−1). At t=0 the Jacobi factor is 1; at t=−1 it is (−1)^m binom(M,m), so no extra endpoint multiplicities occur. Orthogonality gives m simple roots x_j in (−1,1), then t_j=(x_j−1)/2. Newton's inequalities apply to P/t of degree a+b−1, giving the stated normalization. The normalized generating function has independent Bernoulli factors with success probabilities 1/2 and 1/(1−t_j)=2/(3−x_j); the shift is one. The variance is at least (M−1)/4 and M tends to infinity whenever a+b does, so bounded centered summands meet the triangular-array Lindeberg condition. For a=b=1 this gives t(1+2t) and no −1 root. Frozen code was inspected, not run; exact proof covers its test range and all larger exponents.

evidence: Huxley–Lettington–Schmidt already define the length polynomial up to a factor t. For f_a(u)=binom(u+a,a) and f_b(u)=binom(u+b,b), the binomial-basis operator E in §4 has E(f_a)=(1+t)^a by Vandermonde. The displayed general product rule E(f_af_b)=E(f_a)⋄E(f_b) then gives E(f_af_b)=(1+t)^(a+b) sum_j binom(a,j)binom(b,j)[t/(1+t)]^j.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A weak factorization of length u+1 includes factors 1, so f_a(u)f_b(u)=sum_k c_k binom(u+1,k). By Pascal's rule E(f_af_b)=(1+t)P(t)/t. This puts the assigned object itself inside the general product rule and recovers all its coefficients, not only real-rootedness or the evaluation at t=1.

originality.rationale: The full coefficient identity is an explicit evaluation of Wagner's pre-existing binomial-basis product rule, not merely analogous to a different real-rooted polynomial. The classical Jacobi binomial expansion gives its closed form without any new identity for special functions. The exact endpoint zeros are the known degree gap in the same transform, interior zeros follow from Jacobi orthogonality, and the stated distributional conclusions then follow from normalized real linear factors and their divergent variance. This is mathematical coverage by prior implication, not a claim that an earlier source used identical wording or announced the same CLT.
residual_risks: No claim of identifying the earliest source of the exact reformulation or the explicitly phrased fixed-shape limit. The negative verdict rests on a checked general theorem that implies the exact formula, not on absence of exact search hits.
